Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted to our radiation oncology unit complaining of headache, vomiting, and right hemiplegia as part of an intracranial hypertension syndrome. Physical examination revealed a mammary mass in the right breast along with cerebral and lung tumors, bilateral adrenal nodes, and right cerebellar location. The patient underwent total brain irradiation with a dosage of 30 Gray in 10 fractions of 3 Gray per fraction over two weeks, with remarkable improvement in clinical outcomes. The patient was later treated with palliative chemotherapy, which resulted in an incomplete radiological remission of more than 70%. The patient received gemcitabine monotherapy, 1,000 mg/m² on Days 1 and 8 every 21 days after experiencing local breast and cerebral progression. During the follow-up period, the patient's general condition deteriorated rapidly, and they were referred for palliative care and passed away six weeks later.

Treatment:

The patient received total brain irradiation at a dose of 30 Gray in 10 fractions of 3 Gray per fraction over two weeks with remarkable improvement in clinical outcomes. The patient was later treated with palliative chemotherapy that resulted in an incomplete radiological remission estimated to be more than 70%. Second-line chemotherapy with gemcitabine monotherapy, 1,000 mg/m² on Days 1 and 8 every 21 days was administered after the patient's condition deteriorated.

Outcome:

Despite initial improvement following the patient's first treatment, the patient's condition rapidly deteriorated, leading to palliative care and eventual passing.

text:
The admission was for intracranial hypertension from cerebral metastases, treated with whole-brain irradiation, so the principal condition is secondary malignant neoplasm of the brain from breast cancer. That falls in chapter II (Neoplasms), under the secondary neoplasm category C79, with the breast primary coded as additional.

CODE: C79
